Paul Nihill walked beautifully to win from his clubmate Fullager (M) with Eric Hall a creditable third. 4th January 1964 - The Juniors entered a team in the Essex Beagles Open 3¾.

Eric Hall continued his steadily improving form and finished an excellent 8th, 40secs and 5 places ahead of Ray Middleton. Ray Hall had a tussle with Don Thompson in the closing stages and the pair were fast making ground--a few more miles would have seen Ray past several more men.

Middleton did not have matters all his own way though, for he did not take the lead until the second time up Copse Hill. Eric Hall had, until then, set a fast pace at the front. After one lap he was 40 yards clear and at halfway he still held a 6 second lead.

In the Boxing Day 2 miles track handicap, Eric Hall (scratch) won in 22:25 from that ever-present character Bert East (5:25) who finished 13 secs down.

It was ONE-TWO for Belgrave in the Civil Service Championships at Imber Court on November 7th. Eric Hall took the title in 51:39 over this 7 miles course. Second was Ray Middleton, just 9 seconds down.

Eric Hall gave Ray a great fight and finished only 12 seconds down in second place. Early in the race Clark (Poly) and Paddick (RSC) were in close company with our leading two, but the pace became so hot they both came under the judges' ban.

Eric Hall, who continues to support us at every opportunity, was very fit earlier this summer but went down with stomach trouble at a critical part of the season, and was unable to test his form over the longer distances once more.

Eric Hall was a comfortable winner in a very good time, and Bob Barnes showed a welcome return to form in finishing 5th. Steven Laker-Jones was another to perform well and Bob Picton did extremely well in this, his first 'ten'.
Our "local" man, Eric Hall, led home the BELS team to second place medals and finished a worthy sixth himself. Ray Middleton finished very strongly and all but caught his team-mate at the end.
At the AAA 7 miles track championship at Hurlingham on March 27th, Eric Hall (54:20) was 5th, John Knifton (54:55) was 7th and Ray Middleton (55:18) was 11th.

John Knifton was disqualified when lying handily in 4th place, and Eric Hall was forced to drop out---most unusual for him. It was thought at first that these two episodes were the difference between winning and finishing 3rd, but it was soon apparent that the loss of these two men did not affect the result.
With Eric Hall in our team we could have been runners-up but, as it was, Met. WC nipped in ahead of us and we had to be content with bronze medals.
Our own Ray Middleton and Eric Hall spearheaded the winning team by finishing 1st and 3rd respectively; and with Ray Hall placed 5th for the Stock Exchange it was quite a day for the Bels.

We have Eric Hall in Leicester, Gerry Cameron in Market Harborough, Bob Barnes in Cambridge, Bob Farley in Loughborough, Dave King in Bournemouth, John Knifton in U.S.A. and Bill Newhill back in Coventry.

Held on the day of our opening '5', Steve Laker-Jones and Ray Hall travelled to join our three 'local' lads, Eric Hall, Gerry Cameron, and Bob Farley (having his first outing since returning from Germany and joining Loughborough College).

The team,consisting of "Yo Yo" Hall (he goes downhill alright but can't climb 'em) Ray Hall,the chaffeur; Gerry Cameron, the 2nd fastest Scot; and Steve Laker Jones, at present tail end Charlie, were helped out this time by Harry Shields.

Eric Hall shaped well and Gerry Cameron continued to ride on a crest of a wave with another excellent performance. Herding them in close behind was Ray Hall who, although not yet full fit, walked a real captain's race---his 19th position ensuring us of a second team place.
Gerry Cameron is riding high these days and is sufficiently self-confident to take the Editors to task for suggesting that Eric Hall had helped him along at Leicester.

Our walkers haven't the same strength in depth as obtained in recent years but with the return of Eric Hall to the South, and with the help of our two other Internationals in Ray Middleton and Ray Hall, we hope to remedy affairs and build up as powerful a team as ever we have known in the past.
Eric Hall. Our team could certainly do with him again, just as the Editors could do with some more of his "journalism"!

Another to be out of action recently was Eric Hall, suffering from a bad bout of pharyngitis. Eric has been obliged to see a specialist about the trouble, and we only hope he will be fully recovered and fit for the first National events of 1967.

It was too much to hope that the Bels. would regain the 'Berman' Cup for the first scratch team to finish, both Ray and Eric Hall were under the orders of their doctors not to walk and the evergreen Ray Middleton was making his first appearance on his 'home course' for some time - a most welcome return.
Eric Hall, Ray Hall and Ray Middleton have all had bouts of sickness since Christmas but are now recovered and 'rarin' to go for the R.W.A. and Inter-Counties '10' on March 18th.
The redoubtable Ray Middleton is rapidly building up to peak fitness, Bob Barnes and Eric Hall have both produced some fast times and our scout reports that Dave King has been seen back on the road.

As expected, Ray Middleton won the Frank Elson Cup but Eric Hall was always a danger and at one point looked as though he might catch Ray. Both returned fast times leaving Pat Duncan a long way behind in third place although he was given first place in the handicap, much to Ray's disgust!
The 2 mile walk gave Eric Hall yet another Club title and he took the "Don Brown" style award also. Dave King (3rd) travelled all the way from Hull, so desperate is he for competition.

The Civil Service 7 mile championship was won by Ray Middleton. Eric Hall was back on the road after a short break, we hope that he will soon be back on Tuesday evenings to push the lads along.
Most notable for the return to competition of Eric Hall, be a great fillip to the boys to have Eric back permanently, who has lost none of his style and only some of his speed.
